findings.observation: B’s featured player occupies most of the desktop opening; only the license heading reaches the bottom of the capture, with no actual usage condition visible. On mobile, the waveform precedes the sample name and play action.
findings.impact: B separates audition from rights comprehension and spends opening space on the visualization before enabling evaluation. It fails the brief’s explicit desktop adjacency requirement.
findings.repair: Use A’s sample-and-license adjacency, retaining a smaller featured cue within the sample column. On mobile, place the cue name and play action before or alongside its waveform. Recheck that a playable sample and an actual license condition fit together at 1440×900, and the first audition action remains visible at 390×844.

findings.observation: A makes comparison efficient, but its strongest visual emphasis falls on the broad marketing headline and license card. The four distinct waveform silhouettes remain thin strips. B gives the audio material a convincing focal role, although enlargement alone supplies no additional evidence about the sound.
findings.impact: A resolves the opening’s task allocation, but its visual identity is less developed than its controls. B demonstrates a stronger material hierarchy at the expense of the decision path; neither is ready to expand unchanged.
findings.repair: Develop a compact synthesis: preserve A’s scannable rows and decision rail, reduce introductory emphasis, and give one cue’s waveform, use context, and audition action the coherent prominence demonstrated by B. Keep the remaining samples easy to compare. Recheck both widths for a recognizable audio-led identity without pushing rights or audition out of reach.

strengths: The studies materially differ on the named decision: A supports parallel sample comparison and rights review; B prioritizes sequential evaluation of one cue. This is more than a container change, although both reuse the same visual material.
A visibly resolves the desktop adjacency requirement and places all four samples in the mobile opening with clear titles, descriptions, timing, and actions.
B’s coral waveform against the dark surface gives the sound a stronger focal presence; its contextual sample copy connects the cue to gameplay.
Both show controlled typography, consistent alignment, and legible mobile reflow. A supported synthesis is feasible without replacing both directions.
limits: Inspected the four captures at original size in the requested order.
Playback, waveform fidelity to WAV data, filtering, downloads, keyboard access, and selection behavior are unverified from still images.
Full pack selection and license details extend beyond the captures; their completeness is unverified.
